layers.provenance: where content came from and what was done to it, carried as signed records
layers.access: whether a crawler or agent may read or use content, and how that preference is expressed
layers.licensing: the terms and prices for use, in a form machines can read
layers.attribution: whether the source is named and credited where the content ends up
layers.payments: how a use gets paid for, from HTTP 402 to agent checkout
layers.identity: who the agent, crawler or signer is
layers.governance: the foundations, policy bodies and regulation around the rest

stages.at-rest: content or a skill is signed where it is stored
stages.in-transit: the credential travels with the content across a tool call
stages.boundary: a gateway or context middleware checks it on the way through
stages.after-delivery: credit and reporting once the content has left the protocol and its metadata is gone
stages.trust: who may sign or report, and how that is decided. Not a place on the path, but every other stage depends on it
